item.title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
item.description: arXiv:2611.17651v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.

item.title: LHC Based Antimuon-Nucleus Collider LH$\mu$C: Nucleus Options
item.description: arXiv:2611.17849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nucleus options of the LH$\mu$C, an antimuon-hadron collider based on the LHC, are presented. Ultra-cold $\mu^+$ beams, based on the technology of the J-PARC muon $g-2$/EDM experiment as proposed for $\mu$TRISTAN, are accelerated to 1 TeV in either a $\mu$TRISTAN-type booster or a booster housed in the LH$e$C energy-recovery-linac tunnel, and collide with LHC nucleus beams in a 3 km main ring tangential to the LHC. Collisions with Pb, Xe, O and Ne beams provide centre-of-mass energies from 13.1 to 47.9 TeV, i.e. about 3.3 TeV per nucleon. Luminosities and beam-beam tune shifts are evaluated with the AloHEP software. For $\mu$-Pb collisions, the luminosity reaches $2.7\times10^{30}$ ($2.2\times10^{30}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ with the $\mu$TRISTAN-type (ERL-based) booster, i.e. $5.6\times10^{32}$ ($4.5\times10^{32}$) cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$ per nucleon, which a Brinkmann-Dohlus dynamic focusing scheme could increase by a factor of 2-3. The physics potential is discussed, including an extension of the kinematic reach by a factor of about 20 with respect to the LH$e$C, access to parton saturation at perturbative scales, nuclear parton distributions, photon-induced processes and charged-current flavour separation.

item.title: Sensitivity to $\Theta^+$ production in the $\pi^- p \to K^- X$ reaction at HIAF-HIRIBL
item.description: arXiv:2611.17904v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pion-induced searches for the $\Theta^+$ can probe the proposed $N^*(2400)$ formation region beyond the E19 energies. We present sensitivity projections for a missing-mass search for a narrow $\Theta^+$ at 1.540 GeV/$c^2$ in $\pi^- p \to K^- X$ at the High Intensity heavy-ion Accelerator Facility and its HIgh-rigidity Radioactive Ion Beam Line. With the E19 resolutions, efficiency, and continuum, separate 10-day exposures at pion momenta of 2.01 and 2.586 GeV/$c$ give background-only median expected 90% CL upper limits of 0.0293 and 0.0356 $\mu$b/sr, respectively, on the differential cross section averaged over $2^\circ$ to $15^\circ$ on the selected high-momentum branch; the higher momentum corresponds to the proposed $N^*(2400)$ formation energy. Median local $5\sigma$ discovery thresholds are 0.0894 and 0.109 $\mu$b/sr. Nonresonant nucleon-exchange models give width scales of 0.0039 to 0.079 MeV for $J^P=1/2^+$ and 0.045 to 1.47 MeV for $J^P=1/2^-$. All positive-parity variants would test the DIANA width scale of $0.34 \pm 0.10$ MeV; negative-parity sensitivity depends on the variant.

item.title: Curvature-Aware Edge Dynamic GNNs for Low-$p_T$ Track Reconstruction at HL-LHC
item.description: arXiv:2611.17343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Particle track reconstruction in high-energy collider experiments is a computationally demanding combinatorial problem, traditionally solved by Kalman filters that scale poorly with increasing detector occupancy. Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative. In this work, we introduce the Manifold Helical-IN, a novel Interaction Network architecture that explicitly embeds detector spacepoints onto a helical manifold chart using curvature-aware features. This geometric projection mathematically unrolls the tightly curling trajectories of low-momentum particles. Consequently, the network can distinguish true physical tracks from combinatorial noise with good precision. Evaluated on the TrackML challenge dataset, the proposed Manifold Helical-IN achieves a reconstruction efficiency of 0.9675 in the experimentally critical $p_T > 0.5$ GeV regime, approaching recently reported Transformer-based approaches. Crucially, the manifold embedding yields a fake track rate of 0.0037. This represents a 13-fold improvement over the baseline Helical-IN (0.0508). Furthermore, the model maintains good track coherence, as quantified by our proposed Mean Hit Recovery Fraction (MHRF) of 0.858, and achieves a highly efficient inference latency of approximately 150 ms per event on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. These results represent a critical step toward real-time soft particle tracking for the High-Level Trigger (HLT). By operating within practical HLT latency budgets, this geometry-aware approach provides a pathway to recover soft, anomalous Beyond Standard Model signatures such as unclustered energy patterns (SUEPs), that routinely evade standard hardware filters.

item.title: Rank-One Ultralight Dark Matter Response in a Full-Tensor Gravity Gradiometer
item.description: arXiv:2611.17344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A full-tensor superconducting gravity gradiometer whose four test masses carry two compositions in a $2+2$ pattern acquires a composition-dependent channel for dilaton-coupled ultralight dark matter. The reconstructed response is the rank-one tensor $\K=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, with the axis of $\qv$ fixed in advance by the material assignment, and obeys the parameter-free null condition $\K(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$, which no gravity gradient or platform rotation alone can satisfy; it vanishes for a single composition. For copper and lead, the sensitivity reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$, and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers.
item.dc:creator: John J. Oh, Ho Jung Paik

item.title: Composition-dependent ultralight dark matter detection with a tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometer
item.description: arXiv:2611.17345v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tetrahedral superconducting gravity gradiometers designed as full-tensor gravitational-wave detectors, such as the ground-based mSOGRO design and the proposed lunar LANGO observatory, reconstruct the acceleration-gradient tensor from four test masses. We show that giving the four test masses two compositions in a $2+2$ arrangement adds a composition-dependent ultralight dark matter (ULDM) channel to that same tensor readout, with no separate dark-matter sensor and no dark-matter-specific readout. A coherently oscillating scalar accelerates each mass in proportion to its dilaton charge, and the tensor reconstruction leaves the charges only in a mean, rejected with the common mode, and a single vector $\qv$ proportional to the charge contrast $\Delta\abaralpha_{AB}$ between the two materials. The response is the rank-one tensor $\K_{\ULDM}(t)=\gv_\phi(t)\otimes\qv$, whose amplitude is set by the halo, independent of $m_\phi$. The axis of $\qv$ is fixed in advance by the material assignment, so the response obeys the null condition $\K_{\ULDM}(\mathbf{I}-\Pq)=0$ at every instant, for any $\gv_\phi$ including a virialized field with a stochastic gradient---an exact tensor discriminator against gravitational-wave signals; for a single composition $\qv=0$. With the gravitational-wave noise model, the coupling sensitivity for copper and lead test masses reaches $d_{\hat m}-d_g\simeq3.4\times10^{-8}$ for the baseline instrument and $4.9\times10^{-10}$ with upgraded accelerometers. The rank-one factorization and the null condition are summarized in a companion Letter; the present paper gives the derivations and the detector-level analysis.
item.dc:creator: John J. Oh, Ho Jung Paik

item.title: Performance and Stability Studies of GEM Detectors for High Energy Physics Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.17347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: R\&D on different gas-filled detectors such as Gas Electron Multipliers (GEMs), Resistive Plate Chambers (RPCs) and straw tubes has been carried out in the detector laboratory of Bose Institute for more than a decade, keeping in mind present and future high-energy physics experiments. In this article, performance studies of a single-mask triple-GEM detector using a $^{55}$Fe X-ray source with an Ar/CO$_2$ (70/30) gas mixture are described. The study focuses mainly on the gain, energy resolution, count rate, and stability of the chamber under long-term irradiation. The experimental setup, methodology, and analysis results are presented.
item.dc:creator: S. Mandal, S. Das, S. Biswas

item.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Sequence Models for Sample-Efficient Energy Regression in Simulated Calorimeter Showers
item.description: arXiv:2611.17354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Energy reconstruction from electromagnetic calorimeter data underpins particle identification, event reconstruction and precision measurements in high-energy physics. Machine learning already performs well on this task, yet two questions remain open: how much the choice of data representation matters, and whether hybrid quantum-classical models add value in practice. We compare classical and quantum-enhanced models for incident positron energy reconstruction on the CaloGAN dataset, a public benchmark of 100,000 simulated electromagnetic shower events spanning 1 to 100 GeV. Eight architectures, namely SVR, ANN, CNN and LSTM together with their quantum counterparts, are trained on three calorimeter representations: engineered physical features, calorimeter images, and longitudinal shower sequences. Models that follow the longitudinal development of the shower reach the highest accuracy, which points to the value of physically informed representations. The hybrid QLSTM gives the lowest reconstruction error, with an RMSE of 0.294 GeV. Under matched-data conditions with only 1,500 training events, the QLSTM improves on the classical LSTM by 52.7% and also surpasses an LSTM trained on the full set. These observations indicate that longitudinal representations are central to calorimeter energy reconstruction and give preliminary evidence that hybrid quantum-classical sequence models can be more sample-efficient for regression in high-energy physics.

item.title: MID: a muon detector for the ALICE 3 upgrade project
item.description: arXiv:2611.17363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The success of the ALICE programme has allowed to study the hottest state of matter created in the laboratory: the strongly-interacting quark-gluon plasma (sQGP). However, some fundamental questions on the sQGP and other aspects of the strong interaction will remain open even after LHC Run 4. To address this, the ALICE collaboration has proposed a major upgrade of its detector, known as ALICE 3. Among the subdetectors considered for this upgrade is the muon identification detector (MID), whose aim is to contribute to the study of charmonium and exotic-hadron production in heavy-ion collisions. While the baseline design consists of plastic-scintillator-based chambers placed around a cylindrical magnetic iron absorber, different detector technologies are under evaluation for the MID, including multi-wire proportional chambers. This proceeding presents the results of two MID prototypes based on FNAL-NICADD scintillator bars, Kuraray fibers and Hamamatsu SiPMs, characterized in test beams at the CERN Proton Synchrotron with 3 GeV/$c$ muon- and pion-enriched beams. The muon efficiency as well as the hadron suppression obtained using machine learning techniques will be discussed.
item.dc:creator: Jesus Eduardo Mu\~noz Mendez (for the ALICE Collaboration)

item.title: Observation of Non-Equilibrium Phonon Loss Across a Solid-Superfluid Interface
item.description: arXiv:2611.17365v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We measure the performance of an athermal phonon calorimeter in vacuum and in thermal contact with superfluid $^4$He. Using a cryogenic photon calibration system, we show that the superfluid suppresses the collection of the phonon signal by over 99\%. We conclude that submerged sensors will not benefit TESSERACT's superfluid helium dark matter target, but that superfluid helium may be useful to superconducting qubits as a sink for athermal phonons generated by radiation and other spontaneous sources. Our measurement is the first probe of solid-to-superfluid phonon transmission at energies higher than those stably supportable by the superfluid. We discuss thermal flow inside the calorimeter, as well as systematics from an alternative calibration scheme.

item.title: A Double Sided LGAD-Based Detector Providing Timing, Position, and Track Angle Information
item.description: arXiv:2611.17368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe a detector concept which combines small pixels enabled by 3D sensor-electronics integration with gain produced by a Low Gain Avalanche Diode (LGAD) layer. The detector is double-sided, with electrons collected by the cathode, which provides timing information, and an anode with small pixels to provide position and angle information. The cathode can be coarse grained, providing timing with fewer fast amplifiers to limit power consumption. The anode layer benefits from the gain of the LGAD, with larger signals that also limit the power needed. Position can be reconstructed by measuring the pattern of total charge deposited on the anode. Angle and depth of charge deposit can be measured by the shapes of the anode pulses. We describe a possible assembly technology based on 3D integration.
item.dc:creator: Ronald Lipton

item.title: Real-time Electron Tagging by Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy in the PTOLEMY experiment
item.description: arXiv:2611.17369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The PTOLEMY project aims at measuring the neutrino mass and, in the future, the Cosmic Neutrino Background from Tritium endpoint measurement. The Radio-Frequency (RF) Tracker is a sub-detector with the goal of measuring in real time the electrons by exploiting the Cyclotron Radiation Emission Spectroscopy. In this work, an overview of the PTOLEMY project is given together with the design, simulation, construction and commissioning of the RF Tracker prototype: the Electron Trap. The measurements and data analysis of the Electron Trap are presented, establishing the primary path for the development of the RF Tracker.
item.dc:creator: Federico Virzi

item.title: Construction and Commissioning of the Warwick TPC Platform
item.description: arXiv:2611.17389v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Active-target gas time projection chambers (TPCs) could provide the ultimate measurements of neutrino interactions needed for future neutrino oscillation measurements. Their development requires optimisation of the gas mixture, pressure, electric fields, and readout configuration. Warwick TPC (WarTPC) is an R\&D platform for investigating in these directions for neutrino physics and beyond. It can operate at pressures up to approximately 10 bar and features a combination of thick gas electron multipliers and a Timepix3 camera for optical readout. In this paper, we present the construction and commissioning of the WarTPC platform, describing the design and integration of its subsystems, and report the first measurements of its optical response under different operating conditions, demonstrating a stable and functioning R&D platform.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Snape, Hong-Kai Tan, Gary Barker, Alan Burton, Alexander Deisting, Philip Hamacher-Baumann, Xianguo Lu

item.title: Many-body Response to Spin-Independent and Spin-Dependent Dark Matter Scattering in a Superfluid Helium-3 Target
item.description: arXiv:2611.17432v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The QUEST-DMC experiment employs an ultra-low-temperature superfluid $^3$He target in an effort to detect sub-GeV dark matter (DM). The low-momentum scattering of such light DM is sensitive to the many-body structure of superfluid $^3$He, making it necessary to account for the collective behaviour of the medium. We present a first-principles calculation of the DM scattering rate in this inherently quantum many-body medium for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions. The leading consequence of this many-body behaviour is a kinematic enhancement of the scattering rate arising from the Fermi-Dirac statistics of the ultra-low-temperature target. Accounting for this extends the projected reach to lower DM masses for both spin-independent and spin-dependent interactions under the benchmark detector assumptions considered here. The resulting sensitivity improvement becomes increasingly pronounced as the detector threshold drops into the sub-eV regime. It is negligible at the conventional readout threshold of approximately $31$ eV, but becomes significant at the $0.51$ eV benchmark threshold for SQUID-based readout. Specifically, at this threshold, incorporating the many-body response extends the higher-energy recoil tail and improves the projected low-mass reach by approximately $2.5\%$ relative to the single-atom approximation. This improvement becomes more pronounced at lower thresholds. Reaching a threshold of $5$ meV could further extend the sensitivity of QUEST-DMC into the realm of sub-MeV DM.

item.title: Quantum tomography of Higgsstrahlung: Higgs boson self-coupling and $Z$ boson anomalous couplings
item.description: arXiv:2611.18136v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Higgs boson self-coupling enters the Higgsstrahlung process $e^+e^-\to ZH$ at one loop. The three diagrams that carry it project onto two Lorentz structures: the tree-level one, which rescales the rate, and that of the CP-even anomalous coupling $b_Z$, which changes the polarization of the final-state $Z$ boson. To assess how well quantum state tomography constrains the $hZZ$ anomalous couplings and the trilinear coupling at FCC-ee, we compute the helicity density matrix of the $Z$ boson, for an effective vertex that also includes a CP-odd anomalous coupling $\tilde b_Z$, together with its complete one-loop correction in the Standard Model. With these corrections and no other new physics in the effective vertex, quantum state tomography determines $\kappa_\lambda$ to $\pm 3.9$, or $\pm 2.9$ with the full angular information, independently of the rate and of the normalization of the vertex, and not far from the limit $\delta\kappa_\lambda \simeq 1$ set by the quantum Fisher information. Without assumptions on the new physics, quantum tomography directly bounds the anomalous couplings at the $10^{-3}$ level, improving on the existing projections. The density matrix also characterizes the $Z$ boson as a qutrit. At $365$ GeV its state in the central region is pure enough to violate the Klyachko--Can--Binicio\u{g}lu--Shumovsky contextuality inequality, $\mathbb{CNTXT}_5 = 2.06$ at $\theta = \pi/2$ against the non-contextual bound $2$. We also quantify the purity and the amount of magic of the $Z$ boson state, using the mana, the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy and the robustness of magic for the latter. At fixed angle, purity, contextuality and magic are robust against anomalous couplings of the size probed by the tomography. The inclusive state, instead, is neither contextual in this test nor magic in the helicity basis.

item.title: Towards an improved understanding of $a_1$ and $a_2$ transition form factors
item.description: arXiv:2611.18306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The isovector axial-vector and tensor meson states $a_1$ and $a_2$ have garnered interest in the last years since they appear as intermediate states in the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution to $(g-2)_\mu$. Their dynamical behaviour including their transition form factors is poorly understood to this day, which also affects the uncertainty budget of the HLbL contribution. In order to improve the situation, we construct the $a_1$ and $a_2$ as resonances in the $\rho \pi$ system, which allows us to express the relevant amplitudes in terms of known form factors and properties of the resonances. With this, we aim to obtain a phenomenologically well motivated parameterisation of the transition form factors built from the general principles of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Sch\"afer

item.title: The Large Hadron electron Collider as a bridge project for CERN
item.description: arXiv:2503.17727v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The LHeC is the project for delivering electron-nucleon collisions at CERN using the HL-LHC beams. An Energy Recovery Linac in racetrack configuration will provide 50 GeV electrons to achieve centre-of-mass energies around 1\,TeV/nucleon and instantaneous luminosities around $10^{34}$\,m$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$. The LHeC program elaborated in the CDR of 2021 included a phase with concurrent operation of electron-hadron and hadron-hadron collisions, followed by a standalone phase of electron-hadron collisions only. In view of the current HL-LHC schedule, in this paper we have examined the possibilities of a program after the regular HL-LHC program with only electron-proton operation. In this operation mode, the LHeC would serve as an impactful bridge project between major colliders at CERN. The standalone physics program comprises electroweak, Higgs, top-quark, BSM and strong-interaction physics. In addition, it empowers the physics analyses at the HL-LHC by retrofitting measurements and searches with significantly more precise knowledge of the proton structure and $\alpha_s$. The accelerator technology deployed in the Energy Recovery Linac for the LHeC is a major stepping-stone for the performance, cost reduction and training for future colliders. The capital investments in the LHeC electron accelerator can be reused in a cost-efficient way as the injector for the FCC-ee. Finally, data from the LHeC are essential to enable the physics potential of any new high-energy hadron collider. The operational plan of 6 years easily fits in the period between two major colliders at CERN. Similar to the LHeC empowering the HL-LHC physics program, the FCC-eh would be an impactful addition to the FCC physics program.

item.title: 3D software compensation of hadronic showers in the CRILIN crystal calorimeter
item.description: arXiv:2606.05111v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Future electron-positron Higgs factories require excellent jet energy resolution to perform precision measurements of Higgs boson couplings to quarks and gluons. Although homogeneous crystal calorimeters provide remarkable electromagnetic energy resolution, their highly non-compensating response makes hadronic energy reconstruction particularly challenging. In this work, software compensation techniques are investigated for CRILIN, a longitudinally segmented Cherenkov crystal electromagnetic calorimeter based on PbF$_2$ crystals. Using Geant4 simulations of pion showers, it is shown that shower-shape observables are strongly correlated with the fraction of deposited energy reconstructed in a CRILIN module. Simple event-by-event corrections based on the shower transverse RMS and longitudinal center-of-gravity already yield a substantial improvement in hadronic energy reconstruction. A ParticleNet Graph Neural Network exploiting the full three-dimensional shower topology achieves significantly improved performance with respect to simple energy sum reconstruction. Under several different assumptions for the downstream hadronic calorimeter resolution, the GNN-based reconstruction significantly reduces the effective CRILIN contribution to the combined calorimetric resolution, therefore preserving an excellent combined ECAL+HCAL performance. The dependence of the result on the assumed HCAL resolution is also studied and found to be limited within the range considered. These results demonstrate that highly granular crystal calorimeters can recover a large fraction of the information lost because of their intrinsically non-compensating response through software-based compensation techniques, enabling excellent hadronic energy resolution in a combined ECAL+HCAL system and making such detectors promising candidates for future collider experiments.

item.title: Search for the $\boldsymbol{B^0 \to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+ \tau^-}$ decay
item.description: arXiv:2607.25607v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the first search for $B^0 \to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+\tau^-$ decays. We look for signal decays in $B^0\bar B^0$ events produced in asymmetric-energy electron-positron collisions. This work uses samples from the Belle and Belle~II detectors, comprising 1.16 billion $\Upsilon(4S)$ events. In $\Upsilon(4S)\to B^0\bar{B}^0$ decays, the non-signal $\bar{B}^0$ meson is fully reconstructed in a hadronic channel. For the signal $B^0$ meson, $\tau$-lepton decays into final states with a single charged particle are selected. We observe no evidence for the signal and set an upper limit on the branching fraction $\mathcal{B}(B^0\to K^0_{\rm S} \tau^+\tau^-) < 8.3 \times 10^{-4}$ at the 90\% confidence level. Combining this with the recent measurement of the isospin-partner decay $B^+\to K^+\tau^+\tau^-$, we determine an upper limit $\mathcal{B}(B\to K\tau^+\tau^-) < 5.4\times10^{-4}$ at the 90\% confidence level.

item.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Robust Resonance Mass Regression in Cascade Decays
item.description: arXiv:2609.17726v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reconstructing the mass of a heavy resonance from its decay products with missing energy is one of the central tasks that directly determine the sensitivity in new physics searches at collider experiments. Supervised learning approaches to this problem often struggle to generalize well due to the presence of various systematic uncertainties and distribution shifts. Exhausting all possible variations in the labeled data can be very compute-intensive, while a failure of the model to generalize can corrupt the reconstructed resonance widths that are critical in peak-hunting analyses. In this work, following the foundation model paradigm, we use a self-supervised approach to pre-train a transformer encoder with VICReg to learn an embedding invariant to various corruptions, then fine-tune it for mass regression on a heavy resonance with masses ranging from 2.5 to 6.5 TeV and a SUSY-like cascade decay into an eleven-body final state. We show that the pre-trained model reconstructs sharper resonance peaks and has a more stable performance under various realistic corruptions, compared to a supervised model of the same architecture trained on the same augmented data from scratch.

item.title: Similarity Pairing with Energy Mover's Distance for Self-Supervised Pre-Training at the LHC
item.description: arXiv:2609.17738v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many self-supervised methods for training foundation models at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) rely on data augmentations to encourage the model to embed events into a representation space invariant to certain physical or detector symmetries. A common challenge arises from the large freedom in choosing a proper set of augmentations on which downstream performance depends. The implementation of augmentations involves either modifying existing events, potentially breaking the event fidelity, or simulating more event variants, which is computationally intensive. In this work, we present a data-driven method of pairing events by their similarity via the energy mover's distance (EMD), which measures how similar two events are in terms of the work required to transform one into the other. With this approach, distinct events are sampled and matched by their similarity to serve as views for learning invariance, keeping the physics content of each event intact without handcrafted distortions. We demonstrate this augmentation-free pairing method by pre-training on QCD jets via self-distillation and show that it can yield semantic jet embeddings with downstream discrimination power comparable to or better than an augmentation-based baseline.

item.title: Antenna-coupled microstrip summing network for wave-like dark matter searches
item.description: arXiv:2610.36684v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A commonly used technology for axion and other wave-like dark matter searches is a microwave resonator. In such experiments, the detected signal strength depends on the coupling between the resonator and the microwave transmission line that delivers power to the amplifier. In Axion Dark Matter eXperiment (ADMX) and other cavity searches, this coupling is typically achieved using a compact wire antenna inserted into the cavity. While this approach is adequate for right-cylindrical cavities, it can become difficult to efficiently extract power from large-volume, multi-wavelength ($V \gg \lambda^3$) resonators targeted for higher frequencies, such as those designed by ADMX-VERA (Volume Enhanced Resonant Axion). Here, we present a solution based on a microwave slot-antenna array capacitively coupled to a microstrip "summing network," which coherently combines signals from multiple transmission lines into a single output. This summing architecture is adapted from designs originally developed for cosmic microwave background (CMB) detectors. We demonstrate the design and characterization of a new high-frequency resonator that employs this readout scheme in the $19-21$ GHz range. Finally we discuss the potential to reach Dine-Fischler-Srednicki-Zhitnitsky (DFSZ) sensitivity using multiple summing network cavities fitted into a large volume.

item.title: Evidence for the decay $B^0 \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ and improved measurements of the decay $B^0_s \to \mu^+ \mu^-$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00230v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The first single-experiment evidence for the rare decay $B^0 \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ and the world's most precise measurements of the $B^0_s \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ branching fraction and effective lifetime are reported. The results are obtained using Run 3 proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 18 fb$^{-1}$ recorded with the LHCb Upgrade I detector at a centre-of-mass energy of $13.6$ TeV between 2024 and 2025. Their combination with the Run 1 and Run 2 LHCb results further improves the precision. All measurements are found to be in agreement with the Standard Model expectations.

item.title: Measurement of coincident photon-initiated processes in ultra-peripheral Pb+Pb collisions with the ATLAS detector
item.description: arXiv:2504.07795v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Lorentz-contracted electromagnetic fields of the ions in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions generate intense quasi-real photon fluxes. These lead to photon-induced interactions that are observed in ultra-peripheral collisions (UPCs), such as vector meson and lepton-pair production. The high photon flux also enables the occurrence of multiple photon-induced processes in a single collision. Presented is the first measurement of the coincident production of $\gamma\gamma \rightarrow \mu^{+}\mu^{-}$ and $\gamma+A\rightarrow\rho^{0}+A$ in UPC Pb+Pb collisions at centre-of-mass energies of 5.02 TeV and 5.36 TeV with the ATLAS detector at the Large Hadron Collider. The rate of the coincident process relative to the exclusive $\gamma\gamma \rightarrow \mu^{+}\mu^{-}$ process is measured differentially in intervals of forward event activity, quantified by the Zero Degree Calorimeters. The relative rate, summed over forward event activity, for the coincident $\rho^{0}$ production is measured to be $(9.3\,\pm0.4\,\mathrm{(stat.)}\,\pm0.2\,\mathrm{(syst.)})\times10^{-3}$. Correlations between the dimuon kinematic properties, such as its mass, and the coincident $\rho^{0}$ meson production rate, are also presented. These measurements confirm the presence of multi photon-induced processes in UPC collisions, and can provide new insight into the impact parameter dependence of photon-induced vector meson production.

item.title: Phenomenology of the Minimal Scale Invariant Two-Higgs-Doublet Model
item.description: arXiv:2511.06049v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We perform a comprehensive phenomenological analysis of the Scale Invariant Two-Higgs-Doublet Model (\textit{SI2HDM}). In this minimal framework, electroweak symmetry breaking is triggered radiatively without the need for an additional real singlet scalar. After imposing stringent theoretical and experimental constraints, including electroweak precision tests and $B^0_d \to \mu^+\mu^-$ flavor bounds, we identify a highly constrained viable parameter space that accommodates two distinct scenarios: the light-dilaton ($50~\textrm{GeV} \le m_\eta < m_h$) and purely radiative Higgs mass (PRHM, $m_\eta > m_h$) scenarios. Within this viable space, the charged Higgs mass is constrained to $140 \le m_{H^\pm} \le 600~\textrm{GeV}$ while the CP-odd scalar mass spans $400 \le m_{A^0} \le 600~\textrm{GeV}$. This tight parameter space renders the model highly predictive: radiative corrections suppress the trilinear Higgs self-couplings, reducing the di-Higgs production cross section at the 13~TeV LHC by $55\%-70\%$ in the light-dilaton scenario and up to $60\%$ in the PRHM scenario compared to the Standard Model prediction. These results highlight the predictive power and testability of the \textit{SI2HDM} as a minimal framework for radiatively driven electroweak symmetry breaking.

item.title: Amortized Inference of Multi-Modal Posteriors using Likelihood-Weighted Normalizing Flows
item.description: arXiv:2512.04954v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a technique for posterior estimation using Normalizing Flows trained with likelihood-weighted importance sampling, the special case of neural importance sampling in which the proposal is the prior. This approach allows for the efficient inference of theoretical parameters in high-dimensional inverse problems without the need for posterior training samples. We implement the method on multi-modal benchmark tasks in 2D and 3D to check for the efficacy. A critical observation of our study is the impact of the base distribution on the modelled posteriors. We find that standard unimodal base distributions leave spurious probability \textit{bridges} between well-separated modes. We demonstrate that initializing the flow with a Gaussian Mixture Model that matches the number of target modes significantly improves reconstruction fidelity, as measured by some distance and divergence metrics. Finally, we apply this method to a curated problem in heavy flavour physics --- the extraction of the Wolfenstein parameters from the CP asymmetry in $B^0\to J/\psi\,K^0$; it is multimodal, non-Gaussian, and asymmetric in its mode weights --- and compare the results against a well-converged Markov Chain Monte Carlo reference and an exact reference computed by quadrature, using different metrics. Used as a proposal for importance sampling, the trained flow removes its remaining bias and gives the evidence.

item.title: Quantum Estimation Theory Limits in Neutrino Oscillation Experiments
item.description: arXiv:2602.16534v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Measurements of the Pontecorvo-Maki-Nakagawa-Sakata (PMNS) neutrino mixing parameters have entered a precision era, enabling increasingly stringent tests of neutrino oscillations. Within the framework of quantum estimation theory, we investigate whether flavor measurements, the only observables currently accessible experimentally, are optimal for extracting the oscillation parameters. We compute the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) and the classical Fisher Information (FI) associated with ideal flavor projections for all oscillation parameters, considering accelerator muon (anti)neutrino and reactor electron antineutrino beams propagating in vacuum. Two main results emerge. First, flavor measurements saturate the QFI at the first oscillation maximum for $\theta_{13}$, $\theta_{23}$, and $\theta_{12}$, demonstrating their information-theoretic optimality for these parameters. In contrast, they are far from optimal for $\delta_{CP}$. In particular, only a small fraction of the available information on $\delta_{CP}$ is extracted at the first maximum; the sensitivity improves at the second maximum, in line with the strategy of ESS$\nu$SB, a planned facility. Second, the QFI associated with $\delta_{CP}$ is approximately one order of magnitude smaller than that of the mixing angles, indicating that the neutrino state intrinsically encodes less information about CP violation. Nevertheless, this quantum bound lies well below current experimental uncertainties, implying that the present precision on $\delta_{CP}$ is not fundamentally limited. Our results provide a quantitative framework to disentangle fundamental from practical limitations and establish a benchmark for optimizing future neutrino facilities.

item.title: Hybrid neural denoising for resource-efficient near- and sub-threshold radio triggering of extensive air showers
item.description: arXiv:2605.28332v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Autonomous radio self-triggering for extensive air showers requires strong rejection of radio-frequency interference while preserving weak pulses within station-level hardware constraints. We present a hybrid neural trigger comprising a compact waveform denoiser followed by a classifier. The method is evaluated using experimentally measured high-interference background traces and detector-folded simulated air-shower pulses produced with the Pierre Auger Offline chain, with the benchmark concentrated in the near-threshold regime. Hardware constraints are incorporated through hyperparameter optimisation, quantisation-aware training, and high-granularity fixed-point quantisation. Applying the conventional peak-envelope trigger after denoising increases its area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve from 0.63 to 0.98. At a false-positive rate of 10^-4, the full denoiser-classifier chain retains about 41% of the held-out signal traces, compared with 27% for the classifier acting on the raw waveform and about 2% for the peak-envelope reference. The fixed-point firmware is synthesised, placed, and routed on representative field-programmable gate array targets, where it achieves timing closure with microsecond-scale latency and compact arithmetic-resource usage. These results establish hybrid neural denoising as a practical FPGA-compatible route toward radio-only triggering of weak and inclined air-shower signals in noisy environments.

item.description:
arXiv:2606.30135v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the sensitivity of future NINJA-like experiment at J-PARC to eV-scale sterile neutrinos within the 3+1 framework. We perform a phenomenological feasibility study using the $

u_e$ disappearance channels, focusing on possible future configurations of the detector located at different floors of the NM building (B2, SS, and GROUND), corresponding to different off-axis angles. Our analysis is based on a simplified and effective detector response, in which events are classified into electron-like and muon-like topologies and constant benchmark selection efficiencies are applied. We explore different exposure scenarios and assess the impact of analysis choices such as upper energy cuts. We include systematic uncertainties corresponding to normalization for signal and background rates and study the robustness of our results with respect to variations in the assumed energy resolution, and vary efficiencies for key backgrounds such as muon misidentification from charge current and neutral current interactions. item.title: Learning transferable event representations for charmed baryon physics at BESIII
item.description: arXiv:2607.29088v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep learning has become an essential tool in high-energy physics, where the ability to learn transferable event representations can significantly improve model generalization across related physics processes. In this work, we present a Particle Transformer-based framework for learning such representations for charmed baryon physics in the BESIII experiment. The framework is implemented through large-scale pre-training on Monte Carlo simulation samples and subsequent fine-tuning for downstream analyses. Using the production and decays of the charmed baryon $\Lambda_c^+$ as a benchmark, we develop pre-trained models for both event classification and momentum-direction regression. The classification model learns discriminative event representations for the dominant physics categories, rejecting $96.90\%$ of background events at a signal efficiency of 90.00\%. Across 12 benchmark $\Lambda_c^+$ decay channels, fine-tuning from the pre-trained model achieves performance comparable to or better than training from scratch, with particularly clear improvements in low-statistics regimes. For the regression task, the pre-trained model improves the average angular resolutions across the same benchmark channels. Further improvement is obtained after fine-tuning in the representative semileptonic decay $\Lambda_c^+ \to p K^- e^+ \nu_e$. In addition, the predicted momentum direction enables reconstruction of the parent kinematics without a recoil-side tag and thereby increases signal efficiency. For this semileptonic decay, the pre-trained regression model increases the signal efficiency by approximately one order of magnitude relative to the double-tag method. This strategy provides a scalable solution for a wide range of physics cases at BESIII and can be extended to other high energy experiments.

item.title: Open-Charm Vector Mesons in Hot and Dense Matter
item.description: arXiv:2608.04236v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the in-medium properties of the open-charm vector mesons $D_s^{*}$ and $D^{*}$ in hot and dense nuclear matter within the framework of finite-temperature and finite-density QCD sum rules. The analysis incorporates temperature- and density-dependent quark and gluon condensates together with an in-medium continuum threshold constrained by the light-quark condensate. By solving the resulting QCD sum rules, we determine the in-medium masses and leptonic decay constants of the $D_s^{*\pm}$ and $D^{*\pm}$ mesons over a broad region of the $(T,\rho)$ plane. Both vector mesons undergo substantial in-medium softening, with their masses and leptonic decay constants decreasing as the baryon density increases. The masses exhibit a non-monotonic dependence on baryon density, whereas the leptonic decay constants decrease monotonically throughout the investigated density range. Increasing temperature generally weakens the density-induced modifications, although baryon density remains the dominant driver of the in-medium evolution. The largest mass shifts occur at intermediate-to-high densities, reaching approximately $-413~\mathrm{MeV}$ for the $D_s^{*-}$ meson and $-207~\mathrm{MeV}$ for the $D^{*-}$ meson, while the leptonic decay constants are reduced by more than $68\%$ in both channels at the highest densities considered. We further investigate the particle--antiparticle splittings of the masses and leptonic decay constants induced by finite baryon density. Finite baryon density lifts the vacuum degeneracy between the charge-conjugate states, while increasing temperature generally suppresses the resulting asymmetries. Although the strange and non-strange channels exhibit similar qualitative behavior, quantitative differences emerge in both the in-medium modifications and the particle--antiparticle splittings. ....

item.title: TauPolaris: reconstructing tau lepton polarimetric vectors with conditional normalizing flows
item.description: arXiv:2608.10961v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The kinematics of tau lepton decay products depend on the tau spin, giving access to the spin correlations and CP structure of the process that produced them. The optimal spin observable is the polarimetric vector, which points along the most likely direction of the tau spin. Determining it requires the momenta of the neutrinos produced in the tau decays, which escape detection and must therefore be inferred. We present TauPolaris, a tool for reconstructing tau polarimetric vectors by estimating the undetected neutrino momenta with a conditional normalizing flow. Rather than performing a point regression, the method models the full conditional density of the neutrino kinematics, providing both the most likely configuration for each event and an estimate of its uncertainty. The resolution of the reconstructed spin observables improves on that obtained from networks trained with a mean-squared-error loss. Using simulated LHC proton-proton collisions, including detector resolution effects, we demonstrate the method in three applications. For tau leptons produced in Higgs boson decays, we show that the presence of quantum entanglement can be distinguished from its absence with a significance of at least $4.3\sigma$ at the High-Luminosity LHC. We demonstrate an 18% improvement in the sensitivity to CP violation in $H\rightarrow\tau\tau$ decays. Finally, we introduce new variables for suppressing the $Z\rightarrow\tau\tau$ background in Higgs boson searches.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Winterbottom, Lucas Russell

item.title: Neutrino Electroweak Couplings and the Neutrino Fog at Belle II
item.description: arXiv:2609.00121v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The mono-photon process $e^+e^- \to \gamma+\mathrm{invisible}$ at Belle II probes both invisible new states and the electroweak couplings of neutrinos. In this work, we study the process $e^+e^- \to \gamma\nu\bar{\nu}$, finding that Belle II with the full expected dataset can determine the neutrino-sensitive effective weak mixing angle to a 3.6$\%$ relative statistical precision, competitive with existing neutrino probes at other energy scales. Polarized beams, as proposed for the Chiral Belle upgrade, separate the neutral- and charged-current contributions and provide independent access to each, giving a handle on the chiral structure of the neutrino gauge interactions. The same process is an irreducible background to dark boson searches, producing a neutrino fog once the luminosity exceeds 1 ab$^{-1}$.

item.title: Resolving Radiogenic Heterogeneity in the Earth's Mantle with Multi-Site Geo-neutrino Measurements
item.description: arXiv:2611.16715v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a global fit to geo-neutrino measurements at four underground sites (Kamioka, Gran Sasso, Sudbury, Jiangmen), combining signal rates with site-specific predictions of the lithospheric contribution to constrain the quantity and distribution of radioactivity in the Earth's mantle. Assuming a uniform distribution of radioactivity in the mantle, we find a geo-neutrino rate of $S_\text{mantle} = 14.8 \pm 4.5$ NIU when the lithospheric predictions are allowed to vary within their uncertainties. This uniform-mantle signal rate corresponds to radiogenic heating of $18.5 \pm 5.6$ TW. Although the uniform-mantle signal is resolved at $\sim3.2\sigma$, there is noticeable tension between the inferred mantle signals at Jiangmen and Kamioka, which may indicate non-uniform geo-neutrino production in the mantle. We explore six families of models to describe the heterogeneous spatial distribution of radiogenic elements in the Earth's mantle. Each model contains anomalous bodies or reservoirs carrying an excess of heat-producing elements over a depleted mantle (DM) background, with total inventory set by bulk-silicate-Earth mass balance and by a geochemical Th/U constraint. For each model, we compute the geo-response at each detector site and fit the resulting signals to the four measurements. A total of 968,274 individual model configurations are defined and tested. The results of $\sim$3 million distinct fits show that no plausible mantle or lithosphere model applied uniformly to all four sites reproduces the difference between the inferred mantle signals at the Jiangmen and Kamioka sites. Only local, site-specific prescriptions are able to reach the observed difference, suggesting that the Kamioka-Jiangmen tension is due to a local effect or statistical scatter, rather than large-scale mantle structure.
